title: Junctions: Who Goes First
whatItIs: At a junction, signs and road markings tell you who goes first. Where there are none, nobody has priority.
keyFacts: Before you emerge, look all around: cyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians are easy to miss.

keyFacts.text: At a STOP sign you MUST stop at the solid white line, even if the road is clear.
At give way lines you MUST give way to traffic on the major road. Stop only if traffic is coming.

keyFacts: At an unmarked crossroads nobody has priority: go on with great care.
Crossing a dual carriageway: if the gap in the middle is too narrow for your vehicle, wait and cross in one go.

visual.caption: Who goes first at a junction

items.title: STOP sign and solid line
items.text: Stop at the line every time. Go when it is safe.

items.title: Give way lines (broken)
items.text: Give way to traffic on the major road. Stop only if you need to.

items.title: Unmarked crossroads
items.text: No one has priority. Slow down, look and go on with care.

items.title: Limited view
items.text: Edge forward slowly until you can see. Watch for bikes and pedestrians.

a.label: STOP sign
points: You MUST stop at the line
Even when the road is clear

b.label: GIVE WAY sign
points: Stop only if traffic is coming

onTheTest.question: You arrive at a STOP sign. The road is clear. What must you do?
options: Stop at the line, then go when it is safe
Slow down and go if it is clear
Stop only if traffic is coming
onTheTest.why: At a STOP sign you must always stop at the solid white line, even if you can see the road is clear.

traps: A clear road doesn't excuse you from stopping at a STOP sign.
At an unmarked crossroads nobody has priority, not even traffic from the right.
A window pillar can hide a motorcyclist: move your head and look again.
